newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco to de-list Spanish Uniban from Bourse.
newsitem.headline: Morocco to de-list Spanish Uniban from Bourse.

text.p: Spanish Uniban bank, which was recently absorbed by Morocco's leading Wafabank will be de-listed from Casablanca stock exchange in June 1997, a bourse official said on Wednesday.
"According to the calendar set by the Moroccan and Spanish parties and following the merger-absorption, Uniban will be de-listed from the bourse on June 2, 1997," the official told Reuters.
Uniban's takeover by Wafabank was approved by a second general assembly held last Monday, the official added.

Wafabank is expected to increase its capital by 49.2 million dirhams ($5.34 million) following that meeting, a Casablanca market analyst said. Then Wafabank's capital will rise to 6.02 million shares from 5.53 million with a nominal value of 100 dirhams per share, he said.
A Uniban extraordinary assembly approved the absorption on February 26, 1997. Wafabank bought 100 percent of Uniban or more than 2.46 million shares priced at about $28 million, the analyst said.
Wafabank offered one share in exchange for five shares of Uniban despite some opposition from minority shareholders, he added.
The minority group which holds around 7.0 percent of Uniban stock continues to dispute the takeover before a Casablanca court, a banker said.
Wafabank recently said it made a net profit of 242 million dirhams ($25.7 million) in calendar year 1996, up 20 percent on the 201 million dirhams of the previous year.
It said deposits totalled 13.8 billion dirhams, an increase of 14.25 percent over the previous period, lifting the bank's market share to 9.8 percent from nine percent.
Loans to clients rose just over 16 percent to 11.1 billion dirhams, while its mutual funds raised 997 million dirhams, 37 percent of the market.

A private local group owns 50.4 percent of Wafabank. Another 10.4 percent, previously held by French Groupe Suez, was ceded last July to Indosuez Bank group. The remaining 39.2 percent of Wafabank's equity is publicly owned.

Uniban and Wafabank are among the eight banks listed on the Casablanca stock exchange. Banks are most active on the bourse and have the largest market capitalisation with a total of more than 31 billion dirhams, brokers said.
